jobs.title: Project Manager - EV Infrastructure
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Project Manager – EV Infrastructure based in the United States.

This role offers an exciting opportunity to lead and grow an established team delivering electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure projects and multi-site programs. You will oversee projects from initial feasibility and planning through design, permitting, utility coordination, and construction support. As a key client contact, you will ensure projects meet scope, schedule, budget, and quality expectations while building strong, long-term relationships. You will lead multidisciplinary teams, mentor staff, and implement scalable processes that support operational excellence and business growth. Working closely with business development teams, you will help expand the portfolio and explore opportunities in battery energy storage and utility infrastructure. This remote opportunity is ideal for an experienced project management professional passionate about energy infrastructure, team leadership, and sustainable mobility.

Accountabilities

As Project Manager, you will oversee the successful delivery of EV infrastructure projects, manage established client relationships, and contribute to the growth of a developing practice. You will coordinate multidisciplinary resources, manage financial and operational performance, and strengthen project delivery processes to support long-term client satisfaction.

Lead the day-to-day operations of an established project team and manage an existing portfolio of client relationships.
Manage EV charging infrastructure projects and multi-site programs from feasibility studies and due diligence through design, permitting, utility coordination, and construction support.
Serve as the primary point of contact for clients, providing proactive updates on project scope, schedules, budgets, risks, and deliverables.
Manage project scope, timelines, budgets, profitability, invoicing, change requests, and resource allocation.
Coordinate internal departments and external consultants across environmental, surveying, geotechnical, electrical, civil/site, structural, and permitting disciplines.
Prioritize multiple projects and client commitments while managing competing deadlines and delivery requirements.
Lead, mentor, and develop project staff, delegate responsibilities effectively, and establish accountability for quality and schedule performance.
Partner with business development teams to identify new opportunities, prepare proposals, develop project scopes and fee estimates, and onboard new clients and programs.
Build and refine scalable project management processes that improve consistency, efficiency, and client service.
Support business expansion into related energy infrastructure markets, including battery energy storage systems (BESS) and utility infrastructure.
Identify and address project risks, resolve delivery challenges, and maintain strong communication with internal and external stakeholders.
Support successful project completion while balancing client expectations, financial performance, and team capacity.
Complete a pre-employment drug screening as required.

Requirements

The ideal candidate has substantial experience managing EV charging infrastructure or related engineering and energy projects, with a proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and deliver complex programs. You should combine technical understanding with strong financial, organizational, and client relationship management skills, along with a proactive approach to team development and business growth.

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, or a related technical discipline.
At least seven years of experience managing engineering, infrastructure, energy, utility, or EV-related projects.
At least four years of direct project management responsibility, including scope, schedule, budget, profitability, invoicing, and client communication.
Demonstrated experience managing EV charging infrastructure projects involving multidisciplinary design, permitting, utility coordination, and construction support.
Experience coordinating internal teams and external consultants across environmental, surveying, geotechnical, electrical, and related engineering disciplines.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple clients, concurrent projects, and competing priorities.
Experience serving as the primary client contact and navigating challenging discussions concerning project scope, budgets, schedules, and delivery expectations.
Proven ability to lead and mentor teams, delegate responsibilities, establish accountability, and drive projects to successful completion.
Excellent written, verbal, and client-facing communication skills.
A self-motivated, growth-oriented mindset and interest in developing a team and expanding a business practice.
Ability to read, write, and understand English for professional communications and work-related instructions.

Preferred Qualifications Include

Experience with battery energy storage system projects, including site development, permitting, utility coordination, interconnection, and multidisciplinary design management.
Familiarity with electric utilities, utility interconnection processes, power-service upgrades, and utility-led infrastructure projects.
Experience with land or site development, including feasibility assessments, civil design coordination, and permitting.
Experience managing wireless telecommunications infrastructure projects.
Professional Engineer (PE) license.
Experience preparing proposals, developing scopes of work and fee estimates, supporting contract negotiations, and onboarding new clients.
Experience leading regional or national infrastructure programs involving multiple sites or client portfolios.

Benefits

Remote work arrangement.
Company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Paid pregnancy disability leave.
Short-term and long-term disability insurance.
Life insurance.
401(k) and Roth retirement savings plans with company matching.
Paid time off, including parental and military leave.
Employee referral bonuses and professional licensing bonuses.
Straight-time compensation for exempt employees who work more than 40 billable hours in a workweek, subject to the applicable policy.
Education reimbursement to support professional development.
Access to an in-house learning resource offering hundreds of educational and self-enrichment courses.
Mentorship programs and wellness initiatives.
Opportunities to participate in employee-led women's initiatives and philanthropic activities.
Opportunities for career advancement and professional growth through impactful infrastructure projects.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Cloud & Data Protection
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Program Manager, Cloud & Data Protection based in the United States.

The Program Manager, Cloud & Data Protection will drive the successful delivery of strategic product development and innovation initiatives across cloud, infrastructure, and managed services. This role brings structure, accountability, and cross-functional alignment to complex programs, translating product priorities into clear execution plans and measurable outcomes. Working closely with Product Managers, architects, analysts, engineering teams, and senior leadership, you will coordinate milestones, dependencies, resources, and delivery risks from planning through launch. You will establish effective governance practices, remove execution barriers, and enable timely decisions across multiple concurrent initiatives. Through clear reporting and practical recommendations, you will give leadership reliable visibility into portfolio health, delivery confidence, and resource trade-offs. This opportunity is ideal for an organized, proactive program leader who thrives in a collaborative technology environment and enjoys turning complex plans into results.

Accountabilities

Lead program and portfolio execution: Translate product strategy and priorities into integrated delivery plans with defined outcomes, milestones, owners, dependencies, risks, and decision points.
Monitor delivery progress: Maintain a consolidated view of assigned programs, assess delivery confidence, identify potential delays, and recommend changes to sequencing, priorities, or resource allocation when needed.
Establish program governance: Apply the Product Development Lifecycle framework to ensure required deliverables, stage-gate criteria, readiness assessments, and approvals are completed efficiently.
Implement delivery standards: Maintain fit-for-purpose program controls, including integrated schedules, risk and issue logs, assumption and dependency tracking, RACI matrices, decision records, launch-readiness criteria, and executive status reports.
Resolve risks and delivery barriers: Identify systemic causes of delays, streamline cross-functional handoffs, coach initiative owners on governance practices, and escalate unresolved issues with clear impacts and recommended actions.
Coordinate cross-functional stakeholders: Partner with Product Managers to turn product priorities and innovation concepts into executable programs while preserving their ownership of customer insights, product strategy, roadmaps, and business outcomes.
Manage dependencies and competing priorities: Facilitate resolution of conflicts involving scope, timelines, requirements, handoffs, and resource commitments. Escalate decisions when teams cannot reach alignment.
Support portfolio planning and executive reviews: Represent assigned programs in planning and governance forums, coordinate inputs for roadmap reviews and quarterly business reviews, and provide recommendations for resource planning and prioritization.
Deliver executive-level reporting: Communicate program health, milestone progress, risks, dependencies, capacity constraints, recovery plans, and required decisions in a concise, actionable format.
Improve delivery effectiveness: Identify opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen accountability, improve governance, and increase consistency across product development initiatives.
Coordinate partner and vendor workstreams: Where applicable, manage external dependencies that affect product milestones, technical readiness, and launch outcomes.

Requirements

Education: Bachelor’s degree in business, information systems, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Program management experience: At least 5 years of experience leading complex, cross-functional projects or programs within a technology, cloud, infrastructure, or managed services organization.
End-to-end delivery ownership: Demonstrated ability to manage complex programs from planning through completion, including integrated schedules, dependencies, risk management, executive communications, and delivery recovery.
Governance and delivery expertise: Strong command of project and program management practices, including governance frameworks, scope and change management, dependency resolution, escalation, and continuous improvement.
Planning and organizational skills: Excellent attention to detail and the ability to independently manage multiple concurrent initiatives, competing priorities, and evolving deadlines.
Communication and stakeholder management: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to turn complex program information into concise executive updates, decision requests, risk assessments, trade-off recommendations, and recovery plans.
Program management tools: Proficiency with tools such as Smartsheet, Asana, Jira, or Monday.com, as well as Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
Reporting and documentation: Experience building and maintaining integrated schedules, risk and issue logs, assumption and dependency registers, RACI matrices, decision records, and executive program reports.
Product and technology experience: Preferred experience leading programs within product management, cloud, managed services, or infrastructure technology environments, working closely with Product Managers, Product Architects, Engineering, and operations teams.
Product development methodologies: Familiarity with product development lifecycle frameworks, stage-gate processes, and agile methodologies.
Resource and recovery planning: Experience assessing capacity constraints across complex programs and developing practical sequencing, prioritization, resource trade-off, and recovery recommendations.
Professional certification: PMP, PgMP, or a comparable project or program management certification is preferred.
Partner and vendor coordination: Experience managing complex external workstreams that influence product development schedules, technical readiness, or launch delivery is an advantage.
Work environment and physical requirements: Ability to work in an office-based, hybrid, or remote environment, remain stationary for extended periods while using a computer and participating in meetings, and occasionally move light materials such as a laptop or documents.
Location and work authorization: Candidates must reside and work in a U.S. state where the employer is authorized to maintain employment registrations and must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Sponsorship requirements and location eligibility should be confirmed during the hiring process. Certain Atlanta-area positions may require at least 30 hours onsite per week, depending on business needs and assigned location.

Benefits

Annual base salary: Estimated range of $118,000–$130,000, depending on experience, qualifications, and location.
Annual bonus: Eligibility for a discretionary bonus based on individual and company performance.
Healthcare coverage: Medical, telehealth, dental, and vision benefits.
Retirement savings: 401(k) plan.
Health spending accounts: Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) options.
Insurance protection: Life and accidental death and dismemberment (AD&D) insurance, along with short-term and long-term disability coverage.
Flexible time off: Flexible paid time off (PTO) policy.
Leave programs: Leave of absence benefits.
Employee well-being: Employee Assistance Program and wellness initiatives.
Recognition: Rewards and recognition program.
Work flexibility: Hybrid or remote work arrangements may be available, depending on role requirements and location. Onsite expectations for Atlanta-area positions will be discussed during the hiring process.

jobs.title: IT & Information Security Manager
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an IT & Information Security Manager based in the United States.

We’re seeking a hands-on IT and Information Security Manager to own and strengthen IT operations and security in a fully remote, cloud-first organization. Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll oversee Microsoft 365, identity and endpoint management, cloud data protection, and day-to-day technical support. You’ll translate security policies into practical, enforceable controls while maintaining audit readiness and protecting company systems and information. You’ll also extend identity governance across SaaS and AI platforms, improve backup and recovery capabilities, and guide the IT roadmap as the business grows. This is a high-ownership, individual-contributor role suited to someone who enjoys both strategic planning and hands-on execution. You’ll have the autonomy to shape the function while collaborating with compliance leadership and a cross-functional security steering group.

Accountabilities

T operations and Microsoft 365 administration: Manage the Microsoft 365 environment, including Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams. Oversee tenant security, external sharing, licensing, email protection, mail flow, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, filtering, and mailbox recovery. Administer Entra ID, including user and group lifecycle, privileged access, application registrations, password policies, and domain verification.
Endpoint and device management: Administer Microsoft Intune for device enrollment, configuration, compliance policies, and updates. Maintain endpoint protections such as BitLocker and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, coordinate laptop procurement and shipping for remote employees, and securely retire or wipe returned devices.
Mobile access and device governance: Implement mobile application management and device-compliance controls for personally owned phones and tablets, protecting company data on devices the organization does not own.
Backup, recovery, and business continuity: Own backup and recovery for corporate cloud data, including independent third-party backups of Microsoft 365 and Dropbox. Document and test mailbox-, file-, and tenant-level restores, monitor backup jobs, maintain evidence of testing, and review and annually test business continuity and disaster recovery plans.
Security and compliance: Enforce security controls through Conditional Access, Microsoft Defender, data loss prevention, retention policies, web filtering, and DNS filtering. Monitor security alerts and sign-in logs, lead initial incident response, develop internal IT policies and procedures, and track security assessment findings through remediation with documented evidence.
Audit and risk management: Support SOC 2, ISO 27001, and ISO/IEC 42001 requirements; coordinate responses to external audits, customer security questionnaires, and cyber insurance renewals. Partner with compliance leadership on audit readiness while maintaining a clear separation between control implementation and independent assurance.
SaaS and third-party integrations: Manage single sign-on integrations, automated provisioning, application access, and SaaS lifecycle management. Evaluate vendors and tools, oversee supplier relationships, and identify opportunities to optimize licensing costs.
AI systems and governance: Manage identity and access controls for AI platforms, including SSO federation, SCIM-based provisioning and deprovisioning, and domain verification. Restrict unapproved AI services, govern local data access and sharing, maintain approved-tool inventories, support access reviews and vendor risk assessments, and help facilitate annual incident response exercises that include AI-related scenarios.
Helpdesk and employee support: Serve as the primary point of contact for internal IT requests in a remote-first environment. Handle onboarding and offboarding, account and license provisioning, laptop setup and shipping, troubleshooting, virtual meeting equipment guidance, and the day-to-day ticket queue.
Vendor, budget, and technology strategy: Manage relationships with Microsoft resellers, SaaS providers, and hardware and shipping suppliers. Maintain a cloud-first IT roadmap, recommend tools and capabilities that improve security and efficiency, and report risk posture, remediation progress, residual risk, and funding recommendations to leadership.
First-year priorities: Take ownership of Microsoft 365, Intune, and Entra ID configurations; strengthen technically enforced security controls; improve tested backup and recovery processes; expand identity governance across SaaS and AI platforms; and advance the security roadmap ahead of the next annual assessment.

Project delivery and planning

Lead initiation, planning, execution, monitoring and closure of large or high-risk projects, typically core banking, digital channels, integration and infrastructure initiatives.
Build and maintain the project charter, integrated plan, WBS, milestones and resource plan, and baseline them with client sign-off.

The Brattle Group is looking for Research Analysts (RAs)
to work out of our Chicago office.

About The Brattle Group And Economic Consulting

The Brattle Group is a leading global economic and litigation consulting firm. We provide expert analysis and testimony in legal disputes, regulatory proceedings, and business strategy. Our teams apply economic, financial, and analytical expertise to solve complex problems and provide strategic insights for our clients. At The Brattle Group, we bridge the gap between economic theory and real-world application, helping clients make informed decisions in areas such as corporate finance, energy, competition, and regulatory economics.

WHAT IS ECONOMIC CONSULTING?

Economic consulting involves using economic and financial theories, quantitative methods, and data analysis to address legal and business challenges. Consultants work on high-stakes projects, providing expert testimony and strategic advice to law firms, corporations, and government agencies. Our work influences major decisions and outcomes in legal cases and business strategies worldwide.

RESEARCH ANALYST ROLE

Responsibilities

As a Research Analyst (RA) at The Brattle Group, you will be integral to our project teams, collaborating with senior consultants and experts. Your responsibilities will include:

Quantitative Models and Solutions: You'll build models and create innovative data-based solutions for clients using programming languages, such as R, Python, Stata, SAS, Excel, and VBA (e.g. conducting data and statistical analysis, econometric analysis, building interactive dashboards, etc.).
Qualitative Research and Literature Review: You'll conduct comprehensive research, including market analysis, literature reviews, document examination, and writing memos to provide insights and support expert reports.
Supporting Expert Witnesses: You'll assist in preparing expert reports and presentations, helping our experts present complex economic and financial concepts clearly in legal and regulatory contexts.
Collaborating with Team Members: Effective communication and teamwork are critical. You'll work closely with colleagues at all levels, contributing to the development of robust and innovative solutions for our clients.

TYPICAL CASES IN METRICS

In the METRICS practice, you will work on cases such as:

Antitrust & Competition: Research markets, evaluate any restrictions to competition and, estimate any relevant damages.
Consumer Protection and Product Liability: Identify the effects of misinformation on consumer choice, elicit the value that consumers place on particular product features through the statistical and econometric evaluation of sales data.
Telecom: Conduct analysis related to competition, auctions, and mergers within the telecom industry.

RA CAREER DEVELOPMENT

At The Brattle Group, your career growth is a priority. As an RA, you will gain valuable skills in applied economics and finance. You'll discover your strengths and interests, and how to best apply your skills. You will be paired with a peer-level colleague and a manager-level career advisor to help you make the most of your time at Brattle. By the end of your first year, you will have learned to conduct basic research, build complex models, collaborate on analysis, present research findings clearly and concisely. You will have also gained experience and aptitude across industries and coding languages.

THE CANDIDATE

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

An undergraduate degree in a quantitative discipline (e.g. economics, computer science, data science, and mathematics), with strong academic performance. Successful applicants typically have a GPA of 3.7 or higher (based on a 4.0 scale).
Great teamwork and leadership skills. Our project work is done almost exclusively on teams, so it's critical that our RAs work well with others.
Intellectual curiosity and creativity. We are looking for candidates who consistently want to learn more and approach problems with creativity.
A high degree of ownership and commitment. Successful RAs are committed to delivering their best work product, taking ownership of their work, and engaging in excellent client services.

Additionally, We Look For Candidates Who

Have completed or will complete a course in econometrics.
Have completed a significant, self-defined project using quantitative analysis and economic principles.
Can apply quantitative analysis and economic thinking to real-world cases during the interview process.

Autonomy & Judgement: Operate with minimal guidance. Solve ambiguous problems with multiple trade-offs and balance business, financial, and people outcomes effectively.

Influence & Alignment: Align stakeholders with competing priorities. Frame problems and solutions clearly, advising with synthesized data, options, and a grounded point of view.

What You Bring

Experience: 7+ years of progressive benefits program management experience, including direct experience managing regional benefit plans. Proven ability to handle confidential information with discretion and according to policy and law. Proficiency across multiple business software tools.

Languages: Ability to speak Spanish a plus.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an IT & Information Security Manager based in the United States.

We’re seeking a hands-on IT and Information Security Manager to own and strengthen IT operations and security in a fully remote, cloud-first organization. Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll oversee Microsoft 365, identity and endpoint management, cloud data protection, and day-to-day technical support. You’ll translate security policies into practical, enforceable controls while maintaining audit readiness and protecting company systems and information. You’ll also extend identity governance across SaaS and AI platforms, improve backup and recovery capabilities, and guide the IT roadmap as the business grows. This is a high-ownership, individual-contributor role suited to someone who enjoys both strategic planning and hands-on execution. You’ll have the autonomy to shape the function while collaborating with compliance leadership and a cross-functional security steering group.

Accountabilities

T operations and Microsoft 365 administration: Manage the Microsoft 365 environment, including Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams. Oversee tenant security, external sharing, licensing, email protection, mail flow, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, filtering, and mailbox recovery. Administer Entra ID, including user and group lifecycle, privileged access, application registrations, password policies, and domain verification.
Endpoint and device management: Administer Microsoft Intune for device enrollment, configuration, compliance policies, and updates. Maintain endpoint protections such as BitLocker and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, coordinate laptop procurement and shipping for remote employees, and securely retire or wipe returned devices.
Mobile access and device governance: Implement mobile application management and device-compliance controls for personally owned phones and tablets, protecting company data on devices the organization does not own.
Backup, recovery, and business continuity: Own backup and recovery for corporate cloud data, including independent third-party backups of Microsoft 365 and Dropbox. Document and test mailbox-, file-, and tenant-level restores, monitor backup jobs, maintain evidence of testing, and review and annually test business continuity and disaster recovery plans.
Security and compliance: Enforce security controls through Conditional Access, Microsoft Defender, data loss prevention, retention policies, web filtering, and DNS filtering. Monitor security alerts and sign-in logs, lead initial incident response, develop internal IT policies and procedures, and track security assessment findings through remediation with documented evidence.
Audit and risk management: Support SOC 2, ISO 27001, and ISO/IEC 42001 requirements; coordinate responses to external audits, customer security questionnaires, and cyber insurance renewals. Partner with compliance leadership on audit readiness while maintaining a clear separation between control implementation and independent assurance.
SaaS and third-party integrations: Manage single sign-on integrations, automated provisioning, application access, and SaaS lifecycle management. Evaluate vendors and tools, oversee supplier relationships, and identify opportunities to optimize licensing costs.
AI systems and governance: Manage identity and access controls for AI platforms, including SSO federation, SCIM-based provisioning and deprovisioning, and domain verification. Restrict unapproved AI services, govern local data access and sharing, maintain approved-tool inventories, support access reviews and vendor risk assessments, and help facilitate annual incident response exercises that include AI-related scenarios.
Helpdesk and employee support: Serve as the primary point of contact for internal IT requests in a remote-first environment. Handle onboarding and offboarding, account and license provisioning, laptop setup and shipping, troubleshooting, virtual meeting equipment guidance, and the day-to-day ticket queue.
Vendor, budget, and technology strategy: Manage relationships with Microsoft resellers, SaaS providers, and hardware and shipping suppliers. Maintain a cloud-first IT roadmap, recommend tools and capabilities that improve security and efficiency, and report risk posture, remediation progress, residual risk, and funding recommendations to leadership.
First-year priorities: Take ownership of Microsoft 365, Intune, and Entra ID configurations; strengthen technically enforced security controls; improve tested backup and recovery processes; expand identity governance across SaaS and AI platforms; and advance the security roadmap ahead of the next annual assessment.

Requirements

Experience: 5–8 or more years of hands-on experience administering Microsoft 365 and Entra ID/Azure AD environments, including at least one role as the senior or sole IT owner.
Endpoint management: Practical experience administering Microsoft Intune or Endpoint Manager for device enrollment, application management, configuration, compliance, and patching.
Identity and security expertise: Strong understanding of Conditional Access, multifactor authentication (MFA), single sign-on (SSO), least-privilege access, Microsoft Defender, and endpoint security controls.
Remote workforce support: Experience supporting distributed teams and managing device procurement, shipping, setup, onboarding, and offboarding remotely.
Audit and compliance experience: At least two years in an environment subject to SOC 2, ISO 27001, or comparable external audits, with direct responsibility for producing technical evidence and addressing findings.
Backup and recovery ownership: Demonstrated responsibility for cloud data backup and recovery, including performing and documenting restore tests rather than relying solely on monitoring dashboards.
SaaS and AI identity management: Experience managing SSO federation, SCIM provisioning, and domain verification for SaaS or AI platforms, or a proven ability to learn new platforms quickly.
Operational mindset: Willingness to handle all aspects of a lean IT function, from routine support tickets and password resets to laptop shipping, security administration, policy writing, and runbook development.
Communication and problem-solving: Excellent troubleshooting, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to work independently, prioritize competing needs, and explain technical risks and recommendations clearly.
Preferred framework knowledge: Familiarity with ISO/IEC 42001, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF), or comparable AI and security governance frameworks.
Preferred certifications: Microsoft 365 Administrator (MS-102), Microsoft Identity and Access Administrator (SC-300), Endpoint Administrator (MD-102), Microsoft Security Operations Analyst (SC-200), Azure Security Engineer Associate (AZ-500), or equivalent expertise. No specific combination of certifications is required.

Benefits

Annual base salary: $135,000–$170,000, depending on relevant experience and qualifications.
Fully remote work: Work remotely within the United States in a cloud-first environment.
Flexible paid time off: Flexible PTO to support personal needs and time away from work.
Paid parental leave: Six weeks of paid parental leave for eligible full-time, exempt employees.
Healthcare coverage: Medical, dental, and vision plans, including an employee-only medical option with premiums fully paid by the company.
Virtual healthcare: Access to Teladoc virtual healthcare services.
Disability coverage: Employer-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance.
Life insurance: Employer-paid life insurance coverage.
Retirement savings: 401(k) plan with an employer match.
Additional benefits: Access to legal services and other voluntary benefit options.
Direct leadership access: Report directly to the CEO, with an opportunity to shape IT operations and security priorities.
Autonomy and ownership: Build and improve the IT and information security function while working closely with compliance leadership and a cross-functional security steering group.

The Brattle Group is looking for Research Analysts (RAs)
to work out of our Chicago office.

About The Brattle Group And Economic Consulting

The Brattle Group is a leading global economic and litigation consulting firm. We provide expert analysis and testimony in legal disputes, regulatory proceedings, and business strategy. Our teams apply economic, financial, and analytical expertise to solve complex problems and provide strategic insights for our clients. At The Brattle Group, we bridge the gap between economic theory and real-world application, helping clients make informed decisions in areas such as corporate finance, energy, competition, and regulatory economics.

WHAT IS ECONOMIC CONSULTING?

Economic consulting involves using economic and financial theories, quantitative methods, and data analysis to address legal and business challenges. Consultants work on high-stakes projects, providing expert testimony and strategic advice to law firms, corporations, and government agencies. Our work influences major decisions and outcomes in legal cases and business strategies worldwide.

RESEARCH ANALYST ROLE

Responsibilities

As a Research Analyst (RA) at The Brattle Group, you will be integral to our project teams, collaborating with senior consultants and experts. Your responsibilities will include:

Quantitative Models and Solutions: You'll build models and create innovative data-based solutions for clients using programming languages, such as R, Python, Stata, SAS, Excel, and VBA (e.g. conducting data and statistical analysis, econometric analysis, building interactive dashboards, etc.).
Qualitative Research and Literature Review: You'll conduct comprehensive research, including market analysis, literature reviews, document examination, and writing memos to provide insights and support expert reports.
Supporting Expert Witnesses: You'll assist in preparing expert reports and presentations, helping our experts present complex economic and financial concepts clearly in legal and regulatory contexts.
Collaborating with Team Members: Effective communication and teamwork are critical. You'll work closely with colleagues at all levels, contributing to the development of robust and innovative solutions for our clients.

TYPICAL CASES IN METRICS

In the METRICS practice, you will work on cases such as:

Antitrust & Competition: Research markets, evaluate any restrictions to competition and, estimate any relevant damages.
Consumer Protection and Product Liability: Identify the effects of misinformation on consumer choice, elicit the value that consumers place on particular product features through the statistical and econometric evaluation of sales data.
Telecom: Conduct analysis related to competition, auctions, and mergers within the telecom industry.

RA CAREER DEVELOPMENT

At The Brattle Group, your career growth is a priority. As an RA, you will gain valuable skills in applied economics and finance. You'll discover your strengths and interests, and how to best apply your skills. You will be paired with a peer-level colleague and a manager-level career advisor to help you make the most of your time at Brattle. By the end of your first year, you will have learned to conduct basic research, build complex models, collaborate on analysis, present research findings clearly and concisely. You will have also gained experience and aptitude across industries and coding languages.

THE CANDIDATE

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

An undergraduate degree in a quantitative discipline (e.g. economics, computer science, data science, and mathematics), with strong academic performance. Successful applicants typically have a GPA of 3.7 or higher (based on a 4.0 scale).
Great teamwork and leadership skills. Our project work is done almost exclusively on teams, so it's critical that our RAs work well with others.
Intellectual curiosity and creativity. We are looking for candidates who consistently want to learn more and approach problems with creativity.
A high degree of ownership and commitment. Successful RAs are committed to delivering their best work product, taking ownership of their work, and engaging in excellent client services.

Additionally, We Look For Candidates Who

Have completed a significant, self-defined project using quantitative analysis and economic principles.
Can apply quantitative analysis and economic thinking to real-world cases during the interview process.
